The '''Town of Haverstraw''' ({{IPA|en|ˈhæːvəɹstɹɔː|audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Noaius Paticus-Haverstraw.wav}}) is a [[Administrative divisions of New York#Town|town]] in [[Rockland County, New York]], United States, located north of the [[Clarkstown, New York|Town of Clarkstown]] and the [[Ramapo, New York|Town of Ramapo]]; east of [[Orange County, New York|Orange County]]; south of the [[Stony Point, New York|Town of Stony Point]]; and west of the [[Hudson River]]. The town runs from the west to the east border of the county in its northern section. The population was 39,087 at the 2020 census.<ref>U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Report, Haverstraw, Rockland County, New York QuickFacts https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/haverstrawtownrocklandcountynewyork Accessed January 8, 2023</ref>

The name comes from the Dutch word ''Haverstroo'' meaning "oats straw",<ref>{{cite book | url=https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_9V1IAAAAMAAJ | title=The Origin of Certain Place Names in the United States | publisher=Govt. Print. Off. | author=Gannett, Henry | year=1905 | pages=[https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_9V1IAAAAMAAJ/page/n151 152]}}</ref> referring to the grasslands along the river. The town contains three [[Administrative divisions of New York#Village|villages]], one of which is also known as [[Haverstraw (village), New York|Haverstraw]]. Haverstraw village is the original seat of government for the town, hosting the area's historic central downtown business district and the densest population in northern Rockland County.
